payment.q: Which payment methods do you accept?

access.q: How long do I have access to the course?
access.a: Access is for life: once enrolled, you can watch the lessons as many times as you like, with no time limit.

mobile.q: Can I follow the course on my phone?
mobile.a: Yes, the platform works on smartphone, tablet and computer. All you need is an internet connection.

abroad.q: Can I take the course from France or elsewhere abroad?
abroad.a: Yes. Everything happens online, with lifetime access on phone, tablet or computer: you follow the modules wherever you live. The procedures, laws and offices covered are Algeria's, where the project is carried out.

invoice.a: Yes, an invoice can be issued on request after payment. Contact our team with your order reference.

support.a: Our team answers by email and by phone/WhatsApp during office hours, and helps you out if you hit a technical problem.

whySelling.q: Why would a property developer sell his know-how?
whySelling.a: Because he is retired. He no longer operates, he is no longer competing with you, and he would rather pass on what sixteen years in the trade taught him than let it disappear.

modules.q: Do I have to buy everything at once?
modules.a: No. Modules are sold individually, depending on the stage you are at. Discounts grow with the number of modules, and full access remains the cheapest option per module.

excel.q: Is the Excel financial model really included?
excel.a: Yes. It is a downloadable project-finance file, to fill in with your own figures.

subcontractors.a: Yes, directly. These are people the instructor hired on his own sites and kept for their quality and reliability. He passes them on to you; the choice and the contractual relationship remain yours.

projectType.q: Is the course right for my type of project?
projectType.a: Yes. Housing, mixed-use, retail, healthcare, leisure: the administrative and financial process is the same. The instructor has applied it to housing as well as to clinics, a shopping centre and an amusement park.

trackRecord.title: What he built before he taught it.
trackRecord.intro: He doesn't comment on the market: he did the work. Every project below was structured, financed, built, sold and delivered by him, in Algeria.
trackRecord.body: Sixteen years, from the first plot bought to the last key handed over. Everything you'll learn was done for real first, on his own projects — the wins, the delays, the neighbor appeals, the mistakes paid for in cash.
trackRecord.attribution: These figures are the trainer's personal track record as a real-estate developer, as declared by him. They are not the track record of Ebni Academy.

whySelling.label: The question you're asking yourself
whySelling.title: “Why sell your own trade?” — Because he's retired.
whySelling.p1: A serious businessman asks it first, and it's a fair question: nobody hands a profitable trade to his future competitors.
whySelling.p2: The trainer has retired. No more projects to put together, no more land to compete with you for, no more market to defend. What's left is sixteen years of method, files and contacts — knowledge that dies if it stays in a drawer.
whySelling.p3: That's why this course says what a working developer never would: where files actually get stuck, what costs a lot and when, who to call and in what order.
whySelling.lead: Nobody hands a profitable trade to his future competitors. It's a fair question.
whySelling.quote: He has retired: no more projects, no more land to compete with you for, no more market to defend.
whySelling.k2: What costs a lot, and when
whySelling.k3: Who to call, and in what order
whySelling.close: Things a working developer would never tell you.

maze.title: Capital isn't enough. It's the paperwork that stops projects.
maze.p1: You have the funds, maybe even the land. What blocks you comes next: the developer accreditation and registration on the national register, the FGCMPI, the building permit, off-plan sale contracts (VSP), neighbor appeals, mandatory insurance, acceptance and handover.
maze.p2: None of that is a money problem. It's a problem of order, documents and deadlines: a file rejected over one missing paper, a permit that drags on a whole season, a badly drafted VSP, a neighbor who files an appeal at the worst moment, a subcontractor who walks off the site during the structural work.
maze.p3: These are the real hazards of the field. They're written in no official text: you learn them over sixteen years in the business — or by paying for them. This course exists so you don't learn them at your own expense.
maze.lead: You have the funds, maybe the land. What blocks you comes next.
maze.close: Not money problems: problems of order, documents and deadlines. These hazards take sixteen years in the business to learn — or you pay for them.

costOfError.title: On a development, a mistake isn't paid in dinars. It's paid in months.
costOfError.e1: An accreditation file to redo: your start pushed back.
costOfError.e2: An incomplete permit: a building season lost, land already paid for.
costOfError.e3: A badly drafted VSP: a payment missing exactly when cash flow needs it.
costOfError.e4: The wrong subcontractor: site at a standstill, budget reopened.
costOfError.p1: None of these incidents is rare. They are the ordinary sticking points of the trade, and they all land before the first apartment is sold.
costOfError.p2: So the price of this course comes down to one simple comparison: what it would cost you to learn a single one of these steps on your own site, in real time, with your own money on the line.
costOfError.close: The price of this course? What one single step would cost you, learned on your own site.

method.title: The complete step-by-step: from bare land to handing over the keys.
method.intro: The exact order of a development project, without skipping a step:
method.s1: Set up the development company and obtain the accreditation.
method.s2: Choose and secure the land, check the title status and the easements.
method.s3: Run the feasibility study and put the financing together.
method.s4: Design, file and obtain the building permit.
method.s5: Handle the neighbors, the objections and the appeals.
method.s6: Take out the mandatory insurance and join the FGCMPI.
method.s7: Start the site, choose your subcontractors and hold them to it.
method.s8: Sell off-plan (VSP) and collect payments as the work advances.
method.s9: Sign off the works, hand over and manage the warranties.
method.outro1: At every step: what to do, in what order, with which document, and the mistake that costs the most at that precise moment.
method.outro2: From the permit to the neighbors to the insurance, nothing is left out — and all of it comes from a man who did it, not a theorist.
method.close: At every step: what to do, in what order, with which document — and the mistake that costs the most at that precise moment.

anyProject.title: Any type of project. The mechanics don't change.
anyProject.p1: Multi-unit housing, mixed-use development, retail unit, healthcare facility, leisure facility: the accreditation, the land, the feasibility, the financing, the permit, the insurance, the site, the sale and the handover all follow the same mechanics. What changes is the volume and the people across the table — not the process.
anyProject.p2: That is exactly what the trainer's own record shows: the same method let him deliver more than 2,100 homes, two clinics, a shopping center and an amusement park.
anyProject.p3: So you don't need to hunt for a course “for your type of project.” You apply the same process to yours.
anyProject.close: The same method delivered 2,100 homes, two clinics, a shopping center and an amusement park. Apply it to yours.

modular.title: Buy the step you're stuck on. Or the whole trade.
modular.p1: No need to take it all at once: buy module by module, based on where you actually are.
modular.c1: Starting from zero? Begin with the company and the accreditation.
modular.c2: File stuck at the town hall? Take the building permit module.
modular.c3: Putting your financing together? Take project finance, with the Excel financial model.
modular.c4: Site about to start? Take the site and subcontracting module.
modular.p2: Discounts apply on their own as you add modules. The best price is calculated automatically — you never have to ask for it.
modular.p3: Past a certain number of modules, full access simply becomes the cheapest option. That's exactly why it exists.
modular.close: Discounts apply on their own. Past a certain number of modules, full access becomes the cheapest option.
